meta.title: Incident severity triage
meta.description: A decision tree for the on-call engineer: three questions decide the severity of a new incident and who gets paged.

summary.headline: Customer impact decides first, data or security risk second, reach third.
points: Any data loss or security exposure is SEV1, whatever the reach.
Degraded but working service is SEV2 above 10% of users, otherwise SEV3.
No customer impact is a ticket, not a page.

data.title: SEV1: all hands
data.subtitle: Page on-call, lead and exec
data.description: Open the incident channel, page the incident commander and an executive, post a status page update within 15 minutes.

data.title: SEV2: page on-call
data.subtitle: Owning team fixes now
data.description: Page the owning team's on-call engineer; status page update within 30 minutes.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Start at the top and answer each question. The degraded-service branch opens folded; the steps unfold it.

steps.title: Something is down
steps.description: A customer-facing feature is failing, so the next question is about data and security.

steps.title: Risk means SEV1
steps.description: Lost writes or exposed data make it SEV1 whatever the reach: page everyone.

steps.title: Nothing down, but slow
steps.description: Without an outage, ask whether the service is degraded at all.

steps.title: Reach decides
steps.description: Above 10% of users it is SEV2; below, a SEV3 ticket fixed this week.
